_comment: Hand-maintained classification of the DataForSEO vendor tools. A vendor tool ABSENT from this file is not classified at all and gets no pre-approval - the file fails closed. These tools are READ-ONLY with respect to Hiveku data (every vendor endpoint served is /live or /available_filters; none posts a task or writes anything), but 57 of them BILL THE ACCOUNT per call. Read-only and safe-to-run-unattended are therefore NOT the same question here, and this file keeps them apart.
_why_enumerated_not_pattern_matched: The vendor tool list is fetched at RUNTIME from a remote microservice (mcp-seo.hiveku.com), not compiled from this repo. A namespace rule such as 'backlinks_* is a read' would silently classify a future backlinks_*_task_post the moment the vendor deploys one, with no plugin release and no review. An explicit list cannot do that.
_source_of_truth: lib/tool-index.json, which is generated from a live tools/list. src/modules/** in the MCP server is a PARTIAL, STALE local mirror - it defines no serp_youtube_* tools and no keywords_data trends tools, both of which the live server serves - so it must never be parsed as the registry.
_vendorNamespaces_note: The DataForSEO namespaces, stated EXPLICITLY rather than derived. A test tried deriving them from the classified names by taking the first token, which turned content_analysis_* into the prefix 'content_' and swept in 40 Hiveku content_* tools - including writes like content_delete. Same overfit the classification itself exists to avoid: a rule fitted to the sample you happen to hold. These are a fact about the vendor, so they are data.
_second_vendor_note: FIRECRAWL is a SECOND vendor, found by main-hiveku-nosync-ppc on 2026-09-08 and invisible to the namespace rule above because its tools are bare names (md, html, crawl) sharing no prefix with anything. They are served with method:null and are Firecrawl v2.1 on FIRECRAWL_API_KEY. Two things make them MORE hazardous than the DataForSEO set, not less: crawl4ai-proxy.service.ts records no usage at all (the DataForSEO proxy at least calls recordDataForSeoUsage), so this spend is invisible; and one of them is not a read.
_firecrawlMeteredReads_note: Reads of the public web, billed per call by Firecrawl. Same treatment as the DataForSEO metered set: not auto-approved, never swept. They are safe TODAY only because method:null also keeps them out of readonly-tools.json - an accident of the generator, not a decision. Adding a readOnlyHint to md or html (both genuinely are reads, so someone reasonably will) would put them in the sweep, which calls every tool it is given with arguments:{}.
_firecrawlNeverAutoApprove_note: execute_js runs ARBITRARY JAVASCRIPT in a browser against a third-party page before scraping it. It is deliberately NOT in the metered-read list, because it is not a read: classifying it beside md and html would invite the next person to treat the whole group uniformly. It is in NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE in lib/tool-safety.mjs so that even if it is ever marked read-only upstream, this plugin still will not run it unattended. 'ask' is served by the proxy's name list but absent from the live index, so it is unclassified on purpose - classify it if it appears.
_vendorFreeReads_note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, pending verification. Names in here are pre-approved AND swept, so a mistake bills the client on every sweep run. The candidates below are metadata endpoints DataForSEO publishes as free, but that was asserted from published pricing and NOT confirmed against a billing report, and this repo carries no price list. Move a name up only after confirming a zero cost on a real invoice.
_vendorMeteredReads_note: Reads that COST MONEY. Never swept: scripts/sweep-tools.mjs calls every tool it is given with arguments {}, and several of these have no required parameter at all (domain_analytics_whois_overview is all-optional), so a sweep would execute real paid calls. A sweep that bills the client every run is a worse outcome than incomplete coverage. They are also NOT auto-approved: this codebase already gates metered DataForSEO calls behind a prompt (see data/permission-critical-tools.json, seo_listings_scan), and pre-approving spend would contradict that. What this classification buys is that they stop being mistaken for WRITES.
